after.title: Notice of Tenants’ Rights and Resources
after.requirement: Landlords ending a tenancy must provide the Notice of Tenants’ Rights and Resources when starting eviction or declining lease renewal. The rights notice must accompany the Notice to Quit or notice of lease non-renewal or expiration. It must also be delivered to occupants asked to leave, including former owners and tenants of properties purchased out of foreclosure or from a bank or mortgage lender.

evidence.quote:
The Housing Stability Notification Act (HSNA) is an Ordinance passed by the City of
Boston in October 2020
SOURCE: https://www.boston.gov/sites/default/files/file/2020/11/Housing%20Stability%20Notification%20Act%20Tenant%20FAQs.pdf

The Housing Stability Notification Act (HSNA) is an Ordinance passed by the City of
Boston in October 2020 that requires any landlord planning to end a tenancy
agreement to provide the tenant with a Notice of Tenants’ Rights and Resources.

The HSNA requires that landlords give this Notice of Tenants’ Rights and Resources
to tenants when the landlord starts the eviction process, or when the landlord
decides to not offer the tenant a renewal of their lease agreement. The Notice of
Tenants’ Rights and Resources must be delivered at the same time as the Notice to
Quit.

In the event that your landlord serves you with a Notice to Quit or Notice of Lease
Non-renewal or expiration, you should also receive the Notice of Tenants’ Rights
and Resources at the same time.

The Notice of Tenants’ Rights and Resources must also be delivered to any tenant
that is asked to leave a property. For example, if someone is purchasing a property
out of foreclosure, or from a bank or a mortgage lender, they must provide this
Notice to the former owners of the property, or any tenants that live in the
property.

The Ordinance was passed to ensure that tenants and former homeowners
understand their rights when their tenancy or residential occupancy is being
terminated, and that they know about agencies that may be able to assist them.

The Ordinance applies to all landlords/foreclosing owners intending to end a
tenancy or post-foreclosure occupancy of a unit in the City of Boston.
The only exempt properties are residences:
1. in any hospital, skilled nursing facility or health facility;  and
2. in a non-profit facility whose primary purpose is providing short-term
treatment, assistance or therapy for alcohol, drug, or other substance
abuse.
The HSNA becomes effective on November 6, 2020.

Housing Stability Notification Act (Sec. 10-11.7) 
Enforcement Entity: Inspectional Services Department 
1st Offense: Warning 
2nd and Subsequent Offenses: $300 per day 
If a landlord violates the HSNA, it DOES NOT halt the eviction process.

after.penalties: Inspectional Services Department enforcement: first offense, warning; second and subsequent offenses, $300 per day. An HSNA violation does not halt eviction.
review_issues: All six categories were reviewed. The source supports eviction-related notice, City-submission and nonwaiver obligations. It supplies no provisions or explicit negative findings for rent increase limits, security deposits, application screening fees, screening restrictions or algorithmic rent setting; silence does not establish that no such rules exist.
No dated lifecycle snapshot or end date is supplied.
No directional supersession or conflict with another identified legal provision is evidenced.
Official tenant guidance, not the ordinance text; Section 10-11.7 is supplied in the enforcement heading.
The available category just_cause_eviction is used for an eviction-related procedural protection; this source does not establish a substantive just-cause requirement.

The general coverage statement names landlords and foreclosing owners, while the notice example also names purchasers from foreclosure, banks or mortgage lenders. Whether those purchasers are fully captured by the general coverage description requires verification.
The numbered exemption categories are compiled as alternatives. The source joins them with 'and'; verify this interpretation against the ordinance.
The penalty schedule is ordinance-wide and states 'Unless otherwise provided'; the source does not identify any provision-specific alternative penalty.
The retrieval date and the source URL’s directory date are not supported lifecycle snapshot dates. No repeal, amendment or exclusive end date is established.
The source is official tenant guidance. Its reported passage in October 2020 supports the enactment event, but it is not the ordinance text or a current status record.
The statement that an HSNA violation does not halt eviction is a limitation on these protections, not evidence that other eviction protections are absent.

evidence.quote: SOURCE: https://www.boston.gov/sites/default/files/file/2020/11/Housing%20Stability%20Notification%20Act%20Tenant%20FAQs.pdf

The Housing Stability Notification Act (HSNA) is an Ordinance passed by the City of
Boston in October 2020 that requires any landlord planning to end a tenancy
agreement to provide the tenant with a Notice of Tenants’ Rights and Resources.

The HSNA requires that landlords give this Notice of Tenants’ Rights and Resources
to tenants when the landlord starts the eviction process, or when the landlord
decides to not offer the tenant a renewal of their lease agreement. The Notice of
Tenants’ Rights and Resources must be delivered at the same time as the Notice to
Quit.

In the event that your landlord serves you with a Notice to Quit or Notice of Lease
Non-renewal or expiration, you should also receive the Notice of Tenants’ Rights
and Resources at the same time.

The Notice of Tenants’ Rights and Resources must also be delivered to any tenant
that is asked to leave a property. For example, if someone is purchasing a property
out of foreclosure, or from a bank or a mortgage lender, they must provide this
Notice to the former owners of the property, or any tenants that live in the
property.

The Ordinance was passed to ensure that tenants and former homeowners
understand their rights when their tenancy or residential occupancy is being
terminated, and that they know about agencies that may be able to assist them.

The Ordinance applies to all landlords/foreclosing owners intending to end a
tenancy or post-foreclosure occupancy of a unit in the City of Boston.
The only exempt properties are residences:
1. in any hospital, skilled nursing facility or health facility;  and
2. in a non-profit facility whose primary purpose is providing short-term
treatment, assistance or therapy for alcohol, drug, or other substance
abuse.
The HSNA becomes effective on November 6, 2020.

Housing Stability Notification Act (Sec. 10-11.7) 
Enforcement Entity: Inspectional Services Department 
1st Offense: Warning 
2nd and Subsequent Offenses: $300 per day 
If a landlord violates the HSNA, it DOES NOT halt the eviction process.
